key_insight: Patient-specific biomechanical simulation generated realistic imaging variations without training a generative model, improving segmentation across three imaging modalities.
clinical_relevance: This imaging study—not drug discovery research—suggests simulated acquisitions could improve tumor and plaque segmentation without additional patient scanning.
method: Model breast compression, respiratory motion, and arterial wall distension from routine scans.
Use simulated displacement fields to deform images and corresponding segmentation masks.
Compare segmentation training with versus without generated acquisitions.
evidence_signal: Cross-validation and held-out testing showed reported Dice increases of 6.6% for breast and 10.1% for lung (both p<0.05), and 4.5% for carotid plaque (p>0.05); simulated lung motion achieved 0.94 ± 0.02 volume-overlap Dice against real 4D CT.
watch_item: The carotid improvement was not statistically significant, and segmentation gains do not establish better clinical outcomes.
paper_title: Training-free generation of 4D CT and other rare acquisitions improves segmentation across modalities
